title: sculptured.session/v1 line
description: One line of a .sculptured-session.jsonl file: the first line is a SessionHeader, each later line a SessionLine.

ActionClass.description: What a tool call did, classified by Sculptured (spec §6.4). Always heuristic.

Agent.description: One participant: a model-driven agent, a remote agent or a person.

authority.description: The decisions this agent owns: within these domains the others defer to it.

checks.description: Commands run to check the agent's work.

context.description: Files given to the agent as context, relative to the document.

data_access.description: What the agent reads and writes, and what else it changes: its data contract.

description.description:
What the agent does, in a sentence or two: how other agents and people see it when they
choose whom to hand work to. `instructions` is what the agent itself is told.

endpoint.description: For `runtime: remote-a2a`: the agent's A2A endpoint or Agent Card URL.

groups.description: The groups the agent belongs to, by id. An agent may be in no group.

instructions.description: The agent's job, in plain text (often a `$ref` to a Markdown file).

placement.description: Where the agent runs: a selector over machine properties such as `os` or `name`.

skills.description: Skills: a path or name, or the skill itself embedded (`{ name, description, body }`).

subagents.description: What agents this one spawns start as, and the settings they get.

tools.description: Tools the agent is given, or ids of the document's `tools`. Restrictions decide which it may use.

oneOf.description: A typed answer or a chosen option's label.
Permission prompts: run the tool.
Permission prompts: do not run it.
Nobody answered in time (D8): an agent question is told to decide; a permission prompt is allowed.

AppliesTo.description:
How far this block's preferences and restrictions reach. Defaults: preferences `self`,
restrictions `descendants`.

required_for.description:
Actions that need a person's approval first, e.g. `shell`, `network`,
`write-outside-workspace`, `runtime-permissions` (whatever the agent's runtime asks permission
for), or a tool name. An empty list says that nothing does, in place of the runner's own default.

Authority.description:
The decisions an agent owns, as domains in plain words ("wing geometry", "release dates").
Runners SHOULD tell every agent who decides what, and send a question within a domain to its owner.

scope.description:
The group (or `system`) whose boundary this agent's decisions may cross: a decision belongs to
the agent whose scope contains its consequences. Absent: decisions within the agent's own work.

Briefing.description:
`full`: the system's shape, its neighbours' jobs and the working rules. `minimal`: only the agent's
own instructions, contracts and how to finish, for agents that need nothing but their assignment.

tokens.description: Tokens of every kind. A bare number is the hard value; `{ soft, hard }` adds a soft one.

turns.description: Turns (model replies to a message) in one run (MEP-0002).

working_time.description: Time spent working (in turns), as a duration (MEP-0002).

oneOf.description: The agent and everything it spawns draw from one budget.
Each agent has a budget of its own.

CallRule.description: A rule that refuses tool calls: every condition holds for a call to a matching tool.

conditions.description: In Signet-Eval's condition language, such as `contains(parameters, 'rm -rf')`.

reason.description: What the agent is told when the rule refuses its call.

tool.description: A regular expression over the tool's name. Absent: every tool.

Caps.description: What a driver can do. The UI disables controls whose capability is false and says why.

access.description: Members and their rights. Absent: the agents whose connections use the channel.

path.description: `filesystem`: the folder, relative to the document.

protocol.description: Overrides the default protocol for traffic on this channel.

reach.description: `human`: how people are reached, e.g. `{ slack: "#cad-review" }`, `{ email: "…" }`.

command.description: A shell command run in the agent's folder; exit 0 means passed.

Communication.description: The communication mode and bans, at the root or as a restriction.

oneOf.description: Any agent may communicate with any other, except as denied.
Only along declared connections, in their direction, with their details.

Connection.description: A directed, committed line of communication, with every detail of how it happens.

carries.description: What passes along it, by artifact (an output id) or message type.

from.description: An agent, group or step id. A group means every member.

initiates.description: Who may open a conversation. Default: `from`.

max_rounds.description: How often one piece of work may pass along it in a loop.

mode.description: `sync`: the sender waits for a reply. Default: `async`.

pattern.description: Set by pattern expansion: the pattern this connection came from.

via.description: The channel used. Default: a direct channel with the default protocol.

when.description: A condition (CEL subset) that must hold for the connection to be used.

oneOf.description: Work passes to `to`, which starts on it.
`from` sends results or status to `to`.
`from` may read `to`'s activity; it sends nothing.
`from` may assign work to `to` at run time, choosing among its delegates.
`from` may consult `to` and wait for an answer; ownership does not move.
`to` returns approve or changes-requested; changes go back to `from`.
`to` (usually a person) must approve before `from` continues.

ContextBasis.description: Where a context figure comes from.

oneOf.description: The CLI's own per-call total.
Sculptured adds up the CLI's numbers.

ContextCare.description: Limits that keep an agent's context small. Absent members: the runner's own values.

managed.description: `false`: the runner leaves the agent's context alone, with none of these limits or its own.

read_max_kb.description: A read of a whole file larger than this many KB is refused; the agent reads a part instead.

refresh_at_tokens.description: Past this many tokens of context, the agent writes notes and continues in a fresh context.

tool_output_chars.description: The most output of one tool call, in characters, that reaches the agent.

oneOf.description: Each agent starts a fresh conversation from the note it wrote when the run wrapped up.
Each agent continues its own conversation.

CopyMode.description: `own`: the agent works in its own git copy. `shared`: in the folder itself.

oneOf.description: One copy per item of a fan-out.

Cost.description: An estimated cost in US dollars, with its source.

CostSource.description: Where a cost figure came from.

oneOf.description: Claude Code's own `costUSD` for the turn.
Sculptured's price table of OpenAI list prices (`OPENAI_PRICES_CHECKED`).

DataAccess.description:
An agent's data contract: the paths it reads and writes (relative to the document; a trailing
`/` or `/**` covers a folder), the effects it has beyond files, and why. A Runner SHOULD refuse a
write outside `writes` where it can, and MUST say where it cannot. `restrictions.files` stays the
hard limit; `data_access` declares what the agent is for.

shared.description: Values other agents rely on, each with the file that must contain it (MEP 0006).

side_effects.description: Effects beyond its files, in plain words: "sends email", "pushes to main".

oneOf.description: The agent called `record_decision` (structured, agent-reported).
The agent's next message after the timeout (unstructured, agent-reported).
A permission prompt that Sculptured allowed on timeout (D8).
The agent did not say what it decided.

DenyRule.description:
A ban: `from` → `to` (one direction) or `between` (both). Ids may be agents or groups; `*`
matches anyone. `kinds` limits the ban to those kinds; empty bans every kind.

oneOf.description: The same connection in both directions.

Dispatch.description: A workflow's dispatch command: run in the system's workspace, its standard output is the items.

timeout_s.description: Seconds before the command is stopped. Absent: the runner's own limit.

Document.description: A MADL document after `$ref` resolution: one multi-agent system.

$schema.description: The document's JSON Schema, for editors that validate and complete it. It has no meaning.

channels.description: Where messages and artifacts travel: chats, folders, shared memory, buses and more.

connections.description: Directed, committed lines of communication between agents, groups and steps.

defaults.description: Global settings: they apply to every agent unless a group or the agent overrides them.

layout.description: How to draw the system. It has no meaning for execution.

madl.description: The spec revision this document is written against: `draft` or a dated revision.

steps.description: Nodes that are not agents: checks, people's decisions, merges, fan-out and fan-in.

tools.description: Tools defined once and given to agents by id (MEP 0006).

workflows.description: Items passed through stages along outcome routes (MEP 0007).

Egress.description: `deny` (no network), `allow` (any host), or a list of hosts.

EmbeddedSkill.description:
A skill in the Agent Skills format: `name` (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 64),
`description` (when to use it, at most 1024 characters) and `body` (the `SKILL.md` instructions).

source.description:
Where it was copied from (an `https://` address, such as a catalog file at a commit), so a
reader can see where it came from and update it.

EnvValue.description: A value given as text, or a secret the runner resolves. Secrets never appear in documents.

cost.description: The turn's estimated cost and where it came from; absent when no source prices it.

in_turn.description: Counted from one model call while the turn ran (no cost); the turn's last report has the rest.

oneOf.description: controld keeps the message until a slot frees (the run budget's "most agents working at once").
A protection refused one of the agent's tool calls, with the reason the agent read.

Heuristic: the agent has been in a turn with no output for a long time (an idea from Gas Town's
patrol). Flagged only; the operator decides. Its next output clears it.
The agent's context passed the team's ceiling: it writes its notes and continues fresh.

controld: this seat waits for these upstream seats (along "hands work to"
connections) to finish before it gets its first handoff, and whether its handoffs
are stuck. Empty and None = neither waiting nor stuck.

controld: these upstream turns were handed over to this seat as message `message_id`
in the start that began at `start_seq` (its `RigBooted`). Recorded in the same
transaction as that message, so a turn is never handed twice. `resend_of` names the
earlier message this one re-sends, when it is a resend.

wave.description: The "More work" wave this message belongs to, if any.

oneOf.description:
The operator asked this seat to hand its latest finished turn over again
("Hand over again"). `turn_seq` is that turn's `TurnEnded` seq.
The agent (or its CLI) asks the operator something and waits.
`late`: the question had already expired; the answer is an instruct message overriding the agent's decision.
The operator has seen an expired question; it leaves Needs you.

The agent's `report` call: findings about its work (agent-reported). `turn_id` is the
turn running when it was received, so the work ledger can place it in an attempt.

The team's status page, as its owner wrote it with `write_status` (subject: the team). Each
version is kept; the newest is the page. `done`: the owner's final version for the work.
An agent report or tool call that failed validation (spec §6.3). Evidence; never interrupts the agent.
The operator asked for a new session (spec §6.8 handover). A reason is required.
A restore needs the operator: the resume failed or cannot be tried.

The turn ended on the provider's usage or rate limit (`text`: the CLI's words, verbatim; `resets`:
the time those words name, if any). The operator sends "continue" once it resets; Sculptured
never retries by itself. Recorded just before the turn's `TurnEnded { Failed }`.

controld launched this agent without optional abilities its host (an older agent runner) lacks:
`features` names them (`host_proto::features`), `note` says so in plain words and how to update.
Never posture: a restricted agent is refused instead.

A recorded answer could not reach the agent for certain (its host was not connected, or the
agent's program refused it): the question is open again. `reason`: the host's words, verbatim.

The agent's program reports the question settled (hostd maps the driver's `QuestionResolved`).
Sculptured records its own answer or expiry before delivering it, so a question still open
when this arrives was settled by the program itself, without Sculptured's answer. On an answered
(or expired) question it confirms the delivery.

The recorded answer (or expiry) may not have reached the agent: it was sent but no reply came, or a
"Send again" was refused. `reason`: the host's or program's words, verbatim. The question stays
answered; Needs you shows it until a "Send again" or the program confirms it.
A "Send again" of the recorded answer (or expiry) reached the agent: the doubt is cleared.

The model a session asked for and, once the CLI says, the model it reports using.
`requested`: what Sculptured passed (None = the CLI's own default). `observed`: the CLI's own
words (Claude `system/init.model`, Codex `thread/start` result `model` or `model/rerouted.toModel`);
None until the CLI says. Recorded after the session's `TenureStarted`, which clears the seat's model.

Intermediate reasoning the CLI showed (agent-reported). `text` verbatim, capped by
`model::cap::truncate(_, MAX_TEXT)`; "" when `form` is `Hidden`.

item_id.description: Codex reasoning item id; Claude message id.

oneOf.description: How full the agent's context was after a model call.

window_tokens.description: The CLI's runtime window (None = the CLI did not say).

oneOf.description: The CLI's report of how much of the signed-in plan is used (account-wide).
The run's budget changed state: `wrap-up` (its soft value was reached) or `stopped` (its hard value).
Sculptured began running the agent's check command (its design's "check", in its folder).
The check's outcome as Sculptured observed it: the command's own exit status, not the agent's word.

output.description: The last part of its combined output.

EventRecord.description:
One append-only event. `seq` is controld's global order (0 before ingest);
`(host, host_seq)` is the producer's identity for deduplication.

oneOf.description: Plan the remaining work again.
Split the failed work into smaller pieces.
Hand it to the agent or person in `escalation`.

FileRule.description: Paths the agent may read and write, relative to the document. Absent: no limit.

location.description: Where, as the agent put it (a file and line, a page, a part name). None when not given.

text.description: The finding in the agent's words.

Group.description:
A named set of agents that share a purpose and settings. Groups hold only the agents that
list them, and may nest.

purpose.description: What the members share. Passed to every member and to agents connected to the group.

settings.description: Settings for the group's members (and, by reach, their subagents).

requested_seq.description: Set when the operator's "Hand over again" sent this turn: that request's event seq.

turn_seq.description: The seq of that turn's `TurnEnded` event: the handoff's identity.

HandoffStuck.description: Why a seat's handoffs are stuck, in plain words naming agents (never seat ids).

can_resend.description: True when re-sending a recorded handoff can help (it was not sent or not delivered).

reason.description: E.g. "Airframe needs attention", "Planner has no job", "the handoff from Lead was not sent".

Hook.description: A program run with the pending call as JSON on its input, in the runtime's hook format.

args.description:
`{call_rules}` in an argument is replaced by the path of a file holding the agent's
effective `restrictions.tools.refuse`.

Input.description: Something the system is given when it starts: a goal, links, notes.

text.description: The input itself. Empty or absent: it is given when the run starts.

to.description: The agents that receive it. Empty: the starting agents.

Layout.description: Positions for drawing. Writers keep the entries of components they did not change.

groups.description: When the document has a layout, a group without a box here is not drawn.

nodes.description: Agents, steps and inputs, by id.

stages.description: Workflow stages, by workflow id and then stage id (MEP 0006).

Limit.description:
A limit: a bare value is its hard value; `{ soft, hard }` adds a soft value at or below it.
Without a soft value, a runtime may choose one (for example 85% of hard).

Limit2.description:
A limit: a bare value is its hard value; `{ soft, hard }` adds a soft value at or below it.
Without a soft value, a runtime may choose one (for example 85% of hard).

Limit3.description:
A limit: a bare value is its hard value; `{ soft, hard }` adds a soft value at or below it.
Without a soft value, a runtime may choose one (for example 85% of hard).

oneOf.description: The plan's allowance (Claude "session limit", "usage limit", "weekly limit"; Codex `usageLimitExceeded`).
A rate limit (Claude "rate limit"; Codex `rateLimitExceeded`).

max_rounds.description: How often one piece of work may go round a loop, unless a connection on it says less.

McpServer.description: How to reach an MCP server: a command to start (stdio) or a URL (HTTP).

headers.description: HTTP request headers. `${NAME}` in a value (or in `url`) is a secret the runner fills in.

ModelRef.description: A model as `provider/model`, optionally with fallbacks tried in order.

then.description: What to do once `max_attempts` is used up.

oneOf.description: The agent continues with its own best judgment.
The agent waits until someone answers.

Origin.description: How a line came to be: recorded by Sculptured, converted from another tool's file, or inferred by AI.

acceptance.description:
Commands that decide whether this output is done: every one exits 0. A test, not a reviewer's
opinion, is the judge.

Pattern.description: A named shape. Which roles apply depends on `pattern`.

auctioneer.description: `auction`: the agent that runs the auction.

collector.description: `committee`: where members report. Default: the source.

judge.description: `debate`: the agent members report to when the debate ends.

max_rounds.description: `debate`, `role-play`, `swarm`: the round limit put on the expanded connections.

routing.description: `supervisor`: `dynamic` (default) chooses at run time; `static` hands work to every member.

source.description: `committee`: the agent that hands the work to every member.

supervisor.description: `supervisor`: the agent that assigns work and receives reports.

via.description: The channel the expanded connections use.

machine.description: Every key must match the machine's property of the same name.

PlanPause.description: How a run paused at a plan share continues.

max_windows.description: Most windows the run may pause for, at least 1. Absent: 3.

PlanShare.description: A share of one plan window (such as a subscription's 5-hour window) that a run may add.

pause.description:
At the hard value, pause the run instead of stopping it, and continue once the window resets
(MEP 0006).

soft.description: Percent of the window, above 0 and at most 100.

PlanUsage.description:
A CLI's report of how much of the signed-in plan is used. Account-wide: it counts use from
outside Sculptured too.

credits.description: Codex: the credit balance, verbatim, when the plan has credits that use past the limit spends.

status.description:
The CLI's status word, verbatim (Claude `allowed`, `allowed_warning`, `rejected`; Codex the
limit it reached), if any.

PlanWindow.description: One window of a subscription plan's allowance, as the CLI reported it.

resets_at.description: When the window resets, Unix seconds.

used_percent.description: Percent of the window used, 0–100 (it can pass 100). None when the CLI did not say.

guards.description: Project checks that pause new work while they fail.

Preferences.description:
Overridable choices. The nearest value wins: a scalar or list replaces, `options` merges key
by key.

briefing.description: How much of the system an agent is told when it starts (MEP 0008). Absent: `full`.

config.description: Which of its runtime's own configuration an agent loads (MEP 0006).

context.description: How the runner keeps each agent's context small (MEP 0006).

language.description: The language agents write in, as a BCP 47 tag.

models.description:
A model for each runtime: an agent uses its runtime's entry unless a nearer block sets
`model`. Merged key by key down the chain (MEP 0006).

options.description: Runtime-specific options, merged key by key down the chain.

protocol.description:
The default protocol for communication: `native`, `a2a@<version>`, `mcp@<version>`, or
`x-<vendor>-<name>[@<version>]`.

workspace.description: The agents' workspace unless their own `workspace` says otherwise (MEP 0006).

QuestionPrompt.description: What the agent asked, verbatim (capped). Shown as evidence, never rewritten.

allow_other.description: Free text is accepted besides the options.

tool.description: Permission prompts: the tool the agent wants to run.

tool_input.description: Permission prompts: the tool's input, verbatim.

urgency.description: How urgent the asking agent says it is (agent-reported); urgent ones come first in Needs you.

oneOf.description: The agent called its `request_input` tool.
The CLI's own ask-the-user prompt (Codex `item/tool/requestUserInput`, a Practice agent's `ask:`).
The CLI asks before running a tool. Only a restricted posture produces these.

Questions.description: What happens when an agent asks a person something.

timeout.description: How long to wait for an answer, e.g. `30m`.

oneOf.description: The agents the block covers, not what they spawn.
Only what those agents spawn, and what that spawns.
The agents and everything they spawn.
Try resuming the agent's previous session (again).
Start a fresh session; unfinished work is sent with the continue message.
Leave the agent stopped.

Restrictions.description: Limits. Down the chain they can only tighten; loosening one is an error.

RiskFlag.description: A consequence worth a person's attention, in plain words. Never blocks anything.

text.description: Plain sentence, e.g. "force-pushed to origin main".

RunBudget.description: What one run of the whole system may use, every agent and everything they spawn together.

max_agents.description: Most agents in the system at once, its own and the ones they spawn together (MEP 0006).

max_working.description: Most agents working at the same time; the rest wait for a free slot.

wall_clock.description: A duration such as `90s`, `30m`, `2h` or `1h30m`, from the run's start.

RuntimeConfig.description: Which of its runtime's own configuration an agent loads. Absent members: the runner's choice.

project.description: The configuration in the agent's folder (such as `.claude/`).

user.description: The configuration of the person whose machine runs it (such as `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`).

secret.description: The secret's name in the runner's secret store.

parent.description: The agent that spawned this one, if any.

team.description: The team as of the run's start, as a MADL document; null when it was not recorded.

SessionMode.description: How a new session for an agent starts (spec §6.8 "handover"; "New session" in the UI).

oneOf.description: A new session primed with a handover note, then sent its unfinished work.
A native fork of the current session (Codex, Practice; not Claude in M2).

Settings.description: The same shape at the root (`defaults`), on a group, on an agent, and for subagents.

SharedValue.description:
A value at a boundary between agents, such as a port, an endpoint or a field name, and the file
(relative to the document) that must contain it exactly. A Runner SHOULD check it at each start.

SkillRef.description: A skill given to an agent: by path or name, or embedded so the document carries it (MEP 0004).

anyOf.description: A path to a skill folder or `SKILL.md`, relative to the document, or a skill's name.

SoftHard.description: A limit's soft value (no new work; wrap up) and hard value (stop at once).

SoftHard2.description: A limit's soft value (no new work; wrap up) and hard value (stop at once).

SoftHard3.description: A limit's soft value (no new work; wrap up) and hard value (stop at once).

max_children.description: Most agents one agent may spawn.

max_depth.description: Most levels below the agent: 1 lets it spawn agents that cannot spawn their own.

Stage.description: One stage. Ids are unique within the workflow. Which fields apply depends on `kind`.

agent.description: `agent`: the agent that does the stage's work.

command.description: `check`: the shell command; exit 0 is the outcome `passed`, anything else `failed`.

escalate.description: `agent`: after this many rounds here, items go to a stronger agent.

into.description: `merge`: the branch to merge into. Absent: the project's current branch.

join.description: A panel's decision: every reviewer's (`all`, the default) or the first approval (`any`).

max_rounds.description: How often one item may enter this stage.

on_limit.description: The stage an item goes to when it would enter past `max_rounds`. Absent: it is blocked.

personas.description:
The angle each reviewer takes, by agent id: `red-team`, `adversarial`, `simplifier`,
`user`, `expert`, `good-friend`, `ownership`, or the runner's own.

priority.description: A panel's outcomes, worst first: the worst outcome any reviewer gives is the panel's.

prompt.description: `human`: what the person decides; the outcomes are the route keys.

reviewers.description: `agent`: a review panel instead of one agent: every reviewer takes the same item.

routes.description: Outcome → next stage. `null` completes the item. The outcome `blocked` always stops it.

workers.description: `agent`: more agents that can take items here, one item each at a time.

oneOf.description: An agent, or a review panel, does the work and reports an outcome.
The runner runs a command.
A person decides.
The runner merges the item's branch.

Step.description: A node that is not an agent. Which fields apply depends on `kind`.

command.description: `check`: the shell command; exit 0 means passed.

into.description: `merge`: the branch to merge into. Default: the project's current branch.

join.description: `fan-in`: wait for all items, or continue on the first.

over.description: `fan-out`: what to split into items (CEL subset), e.g. `inputs.parts`.

template.description: What a spawned agent starts as. Its `id` is assigned at run time and is not given here.

budget.description: What one run of the whole system may use (MEP-0002).

id.description: Stable identifier: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter or digit.

ThinkingForm.description: What the CLI showed of a model's thinking.

oneOf.description: A summary of the reasoning (Claude thinking summaries, Codex reasoning summary).
The reasoning text itself.
Thinking happened but the CLI returned no text.

TokenCount.description: Which tokens count toward a token limit.

oneOf.description: Input, output, cache reads and cache writes.
Everything except cache reads.

Tool.description:
What an agent is given beyond its instructions. At most one of `mcp`, `builtin`, `hook`,
`plugin` and `skills` says what it is; with none, the id names a tool the runner provides.

builtin.description: A runtime's own tool, as `<runtime>:<name>`, e.g. `claude-code:Bash`.

hook.description: A program the runner calls before each of the agent's tool calls; it may refuse the call.

install.description: How to set it up on a machine, for the person running the system.

instructions.description: What agents given the tool are told about it.

plugin.description: A plugin installed for the agent's runtime, as `name@marketplace`.

requires.description: Other tools it needs, by id; an agent given this one is given them too.

runtimes.description: The runtimes it works with. Empty: any.

skills.description: Skills added to the agent's own; nothing runs.

ToolRef.description:
A tool given to an agent: the tool itself, or the id of one of the document's `tools` (or of a
tool the runner provides).

ToolRule.description:
`allow`: only these tools (absent: every tool the agent is given). `deny`: never these.
Tools are named by tool id, `<tool id>/<tool name>` for one MCP tool, or `<runtime>:<name>`.

refuse.description: Rules that refuse single calls; the first that matches refuses (MEP 0006).

patterns.description: Shorthand that expands into connections (and, for `blackboard`, a channel).

Urgency.description: An agent's own word on how much a question holds up (an idea from Gas Town's escalation severity).

oneOf.description: A preference it could decide itself.
The work cannot go on, or others wait on the answer.

Wave.description:
A wave of "More work": started by one agent's finished work (or a "Hand over again"
press on it), it runs every agent downstream of that origin once.

id.description: The seq of the event that started it: the origin's `TurnEnded` or its `HandoverRequested`.

origin.description: The seat the wave started at.

collector.description: The agent that assembles the completed items.

copies.description: `per-item`: each item gets its own git copy. Absent: `shared`.

dispatch.description:
A command whose output is the items, run by the runner when the system starts, in place of a
dispatcher agent.

dispatcher.description:
The agent that splits the input into items and hands each to the entry stage. A workflow names
either a `dispatcher` or a `dispatch` command (`workflow-dispatch`).

entry.description: The stage every item starts at.

input.description: The input the dispatcher splits, by id.

max_items.description: Most items one run may make. Absent: the runner's own limit.

max_steps.description: Most steps one item may take through the stages. Absent: the runner's own limit.

folder.description: The agent's working folder, relative to the document.
